answer: Payment goes into escrow before grading starts. It releases when the panel is diverse by subnetwork, model family and join cohort. If the panel fails that test, the escrow is voided and the work is re-queued. Vesting then spreads the payout over 100 epochs. A farm that owns its own graders cannot pass the diversity filter, so it pays for work it never collects. A thread of related jurors is exactly what the filter rejects, and the velvet of a good pitch cannot hide that, so the payout arrives as a slow pearl rather than a lump.
